purpose: Cross-domain expansion pack for the Atlas. Each record is designed to become a canonical node or a relationship family rather than an isolated fact.

energy.name: European Energy System
energy.definition: Interconnected electricity, gas, oil, nuclear, renewables, storage, grids, markets and demand across Europe.

energy.name: North Sea Offshore Wind
energy.definition: Offshore wind generation and associated grid, port, vessel, cable and industrial supply-chain systems around the North Sea.

energy.name: European Power Grid
energy.definition: Synchronous and interconnected electricity networks linking national transmission systems through cross-border interconnectors.

energy.name: Liquefied Natural Gas
energy.definition: Globally traded natural gas shipped as a cryogenic liquid and regasified near demand centres.

energy.name: Nuclear Energy
energy.definition: Electricity and heat production using nuclear fission, with fuel-cycle, reactor, waste and regulatory dependencies.

energy.name: Hydrogen Economy
energy.definition: Production, transport, storage and industrial use of hydrogen and derivatives such as ammonia.

finance.name: Public Finance and Debt
finance.definition: Government revenue, expenditure, deficits, debt issuance, interest costs, guarantees and fiscal rules.

finance.name: Sovereign Bond Markets
finance.definition: Markets in government debt securities linking states, banks, funds, households and central banks.

finance.name: European Banking System
finance.definition: Banks, central counterparties, payment systems, deposit protection, regulators and credit channels.

finance.name: Capital Markets Union
finance.definition: EU effort to deepen cross-border capital markets and diversify financing beyond bank credit.

finance.name: Sustainable Finance
finance.definition: Financial products, disclosure rules and capital-allocation frameworks relating to environmental and social risks.

trade-logistics.name: European Port System
trade-logistics.definition: Ports, terminals, shipping lines, hinterland rail/road connections, customs and logistics networks.

trade-logistics.name: Container Shipping
trade-logistics.definition: Intermodal freight system connecting manufacturers, ports, shipping companies, warehouses and consumers.

trade-logistics.name: European Rail Freight
trade-logistics.definition: Cross-border freight rail corridors and terminals connecting industrial regions and ports.

trade-logistics.name: North Sea
trade-logistics.definition: Marine region linking the UK, Norway, Denmark, Germany, Netherlands, Belgium and France through ecology, energy, shipping and security.

trade-logistics.name: Arctic Shipping
trade-logistics.definition: Maritime transport routes and infrastructure affected by Arctic geography, ice conditions, sovereignty and environmental constraints.

technology.name: Semiconductor Supply Chain
technology.definition: Design, fabrication, equipment, materials, packaging and distribution networks underpinning modern electronics.

technology.name: Cloud Computing
technology.definition: Distributed compute, storage, networking and platform services supplied through large data-centre and software ecosystems.

technology.name: Artificial Intelligence
technology.definition: Machine-learning and related computational systems used for prediction, generation, optimization, automation and decision support.

technology.name: Cybersecurity
technology.definition: Technologies, institutions and practices protecting information systems, networks and critical infrastructure.

technology.name: Subsea Cable Network
technology.definition: Undersea telecommunications cables carrying a major share of intercontinental data traffic.

technology.name: Satellite Infrastructure
technology.definition: Launch, satellite, ground-station and communications systems supporting navigation, Earth observation, communications and intelligence.

institutions.name: North Atlantic Treaty Organization
institutions.definition: Collective-defence alliance linking European and North American members.

institutions.name: United Nations
institutions.definition: Global intergovernmental organization covering peace and security, development, humanitarian affairs and international law.

institutions.name: World Trade Organization
institutions.definition: International institution governing a multilateral trade-rule framework.

institutions.name: International Monetary Fund
institutions.definition: International financial institution focused on monetary cooperation, balance-of-payments support and macroeconomic surveillance.

institutions.name: World Bank Group
institutions.definition: Development-finance institutions providing loans, grants, research and policy support.

institutions.name: OECD
institutions.definition: Intergovernmental organization producing comparative economic, tax, education and policy analysis.

institutions.name: OSCE
institutions.definition: Regional security organization focused on conflict prevention, arms control, human rights and field missions.

society.name: Demography
society.definition: Population size, age structure, fertility, mortality, migration, households and spatial distribution.

society.name: Migration System
society.definition: Flows and stocks of people moving across borders or within states, shaped by work, family, conflict, law and opportunity.

society.name: Labour Market
society.definition: Workers, employers, skills, wages, participation, unemployment, migration and institutions governing employment.

society.name: Healthcare System
society.definition: Institutions, professionals, financing, medicines, infrastructure and services used to maintain population health.

society.name: Education System
society.definition: Schools, universities, vocational systems, teachers, students, credentials and research institutions.

society.name: Housing System
society.definition: Housing stock, construction, rents, mortgages, land, planning rules and household affordability.

governance.name: Public Procurement
governance.definition: Government purchasing of goods, services and works through contracts, tenders, frameworks and supplier relationships.

governance.name: Tax Expenditures
governance.definition: Revenue foregone through exemptions, deductions, credits, reduced rates and preferential treatments.

governance.name: Subsidy System
governance.definition: Transfers or financial advantages provided by governments to households, firms, sectors or regions.

governance.name: Regulatory System
governance.definition: Rules, regulators, licensing, enforcement and compliance mechanisms shaping economic and social activity.

governance.name: Pension System
governance.definition: Public and private arrangements transferring income across working life and retirement.

security.name: Counterterrorism System
security.definition: Law-enforcement, intelligence, border, financial, judicial and prevention mechanisms used to counter terrorism.

security.name: Counterintelligence System
security.definition: Institutions and practices intended to detect, deter and disrupt foreign intelligence activity and espionage.

security.name: Financial Intelligence
security.definition: Collection and analysis of financial transaction information for detecting money laundering, terrorist financing and related crime.

security.name: Border Security
security.definition: Institutions, infrastructure, customs, immigration and information systems controlling movement across borders.

security.name: Critical Infrastructure Protection
security.definition: Protection and resilience of energy, transport, communications, water, finance, health and other essential systems.
